steps.tx: **Wernicke encephalopathy** is an acute, life-threatening neuropsychiatric emergency caused by severe thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency, characteristically encountered in chronic alcohol dependence and severe nutritional deprivation. The classic clinical presentation features a triad of global confusion, cerebellar ataxia, and bilateral ophthalmoplegia with nystagmus.
steps.say: Wernicke encephalopathy is an acute medical emergency from thiamine deficiency, classically presenting with confusion, ataxia, and ocular motor palsies.

left.title: Classic Clinical Triad
points: Global mental confusion & disorientation
Truncal & gait cerebellar ataxia
Bilateral abducens palsy (CN VI)
Horizontal & vertical nystagmus

right.title: Diagnostic Reality
points: Full triad present in only thirty percent
Confusion is the most frequent sign
Petechial hemorrhages in mammillary bodies
Rapidly fatal if untreated with thiamine

steps.tx: Brain magnetic resonance imaging in acute Wernicke encephalopathy demonstrates characteristic selective vulnerability of periventricular structures lacking adequate thiamine pyrophosphate. Symmetrical **mammillary body hyperintensity** on T2-weighted and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences, alongside signal abnormalities within the dorsomedial thalamus and periaqueductal gray matter, confirms acute neurotoxicity. Prompt intravenous thiamine must precede glucose administration to prevent irreversible necrosis.
steps.say: Mammillary body hyperintensity and medial thalamic signal changes on T2-weighted MRI confirm acute Wernicke encephalopathy requiring urgent parenteral thiamine.

vis.alt: Axial brain scan showing bright signal in mammillary bodies and medial thalamus.
vis.caption: Axial brain scan showing bright signal in mammillary bodies and medial thalamus, matching Wernicke changes from severe thiamine depletion. Brain MRI shows bright thiamine deficiency changes in midbrain. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Neuropathology of Wernicke encephalopathy** demonstrates selective microvascular congestion, petechial haemorrhages, and glial proliferation within periventricular diencephalic structures. Vulnerable regions include the mammillary bodies, periaqueductal grey matter of the midbrain, and the dorsomedial and anterior nuclei of the thalamus, reflecting their high rate of thiamine-dependent glucose metabolism.
steps.say: Microscopic pathology reveals petechial hemorrhages and capillary endothelial proliferation in the mammillary bodies, thalamus, and midbrain periaqueductal gray.

vis.title: Neuropathological Distribution
rows: Acute confusion and transitional amnesic deficits
Vestibular dysfunction and severe truncal ataxia

steps.tx: **Parenteral thiamine treatment protocol** requires immediate intravenous or intramuscular administration of high-dose thiamine (500 milligrams three times daily) diluted in normal saline over 30 minutes for three consecutive days. Oral thiamine is completely ineffective in acute Wernicke encephalopathy due to alcohol-induced mucosal malabsorption.
steps.say: Acute Wernicke encephalopathy demands immediate high-dose parenteral thiamine of five hundred milligrams three times daily. Oral thiamine fails due to malabsorption.

nodes.label: Identify clinical signs: confusion, nystagmus, or ataxia
Administer IV thiamine 500 mg infused over 30 minutes
Continue thiamine 500 mg IV three times daily for 3 days
Step down to 250 mg daily until full cognitive stabilization

steps.tx: **Lorazepam pharmacokinetics in hepatic cirrhosis** make it the undisputed sedative of choice for alcohol withdrawal in patients with chronic liver disease, alcoholic hepatitis, or cirrhosis. Unlike chlordiazepoxide, lorazepam bypasses Phase I hepatic cytochrome P450 oxidation, undergoing direct Phase II glucuronidation to form an inactive water-soluble conjugate.
steps.say: Lorazepam is the sedative of choice in liver cirrhosis because it undergoes direct glucuronidation without relying on hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes.

vis.alt: Lorazepam Phase II hepatic glucuronidation pathway preserving clearance in cirrhotic liver disease
vis.caption: Lorazepam Phase II hepatic glucuronidation pathway preserving clearance in cirrhotic liver disease.

steps.tx: **Korsakoff psychosis** represents the chronic, largely irreversible neurocognitive sequel of untreated or inadequately treated Wernicke encephalopathy. Characterized by profound anterograde amnesia, extensive retrograde memory loss, and lack of illness insight, patients retain completely intact immediate working memory and alert clear sensorium.
steps.say: Korsakoff psychosis is the chronic irreversible sequel of thiamine deficiency, causing profound anterograde amnesia while immediate working memory remains intact.

left.title: Memory Profile
points: Profound anterograde amnesia (cannot learn new facts)
Variable retrograde amnesia for remote events
Immediate working memory completely intact
Procedural motor memory well preserved

right.title: Cognitive Features
points: Alert, completely clear level of consciousness
Preserved general intelligence quotient
Prominent confabulation to fill memory voids
Total lack of insight into memory disability

steps.tx: **Confabulation** is the hallmark clinical phenomenon of Korsakoff amnesia, involving the spontaneous or provoked fabrication of detailed, false memories to bridge extensive autobiographical memory gaps. Crucially, confabulation occurs without any conscious intent to deceive; patients genuinely believe their fabricated narrative as absolute truth.
steps.say: Confabulation involves fabricating memories to bridge gaps without intent to deceive. Patients genuinely believe their invented stories to be completely true.

left.title: Spontaneous Confabulation
points: Unprovoked fantastical narrative claims
Associated with frontal lobe executive lesions
Loss of self-monitoring and memory verification
Prominent in early stages of Korsakoff

right.title: Provoked Confabulation
points: Elicited by direct clinician questioning
Plausible everyday fabrications produced
Compensatory mechanism to mask memory void
Persists indefinitely throughout chronic course

steps.tx: **Diagnostic differentiation of amnesias** distinguishes Korsakoff amnesia from Alzheimer disease and transient global amnesia based on specific neuropsychological profiles. In Korsakoff amnesia, immediate registration remains normal while delayed recall is devastated; Alzheimer disease presents with pervasive global cortical deterioration including aphasia and apraxia.
steps.say: Korsakoff amnesia spares immediate registration while devastating delayed recall. Alzheimer disease causes generalized cortical decline with aphasia and apraxia.

steps.tx: **Long-term recovery prospects** in Korsakoff syndrome remain poor: only approximately 20 percent of affected patients achieve complete recovery of functional memory, while 25 percent show no improvement whatsoever. Continued complete alcohol abstinence and lifelong oral thiamine supplementation are mandatory to halt further neurological deterioration.
steps.say: Only twenty percent of Korsakoff patients recover memory function. Strict lifelong alcohol abstinence and thiamine are required to halt further damage.

vis.title: Korsakoff Prognostic Outcomes
rows: Near-total restoration of memory encoding capacity
Meaningful recovery; requires structured daily reminders
Minor improvements; remains institutionalized or dependent
Severe permanent disability; total memory dependency
